proof_summary: Writing a composite \(n=2^e m\), an odd prime divisor \(p\mid m\) is handled by selecting the factors \(2^{(p-1)j}-1\) and applying LTE to show that enough \(p\)-adic valuation survives division by \((n-1)!\), forcing \(p\mid a(n-1)\) and hence impossibly \(p\mid2^{n-2}\); the pure power-of-two case is excluded by the exact value \(v_2(a(2^e-1))=e-1\). For prime \(p\), reduction modulo \(p\) and Wilson’s theorem turn the hypothesis into \(\prod_{1\le k<p-1}(2^k-1)=1\), so none of the powers \(2^k\) with \(0<k<p-1\) equals \(1\), while Fermat’s theorem gives \(2^{p-1}=1\), proving that the order is exactly \(p-1\).
